answer: Attention Decay Ledger. Each identity must publish a signed heartbeat every epoch; missing one lowers its reach score toward a nadir, and only continuous presence rebuilds it. An attacker needs one live agent-session per identity, paid in compute and monitoring hours, so mass identities cost sustained attention rather than a one-time fee. Reach recovery is slow and linear, like regrowth across a meadow, giving no shortcut. A quartz-stable clock enforces epochs, preventing backdated heartbeats.
